sections.heading: The setup
sections.body: The S&P 500 closed Nov 18 at 7,323.63, its lowest close of the past month and 5.6% under the Oct 21 high. The Nasdaq 100 is at 27,116.26, 9.1% below that same peak and 1.8% above its Nov 5 low. Euro Stoxx 50 is flat over the month (+0.2%) and 3.8% under its Nov 12 high. VIX closed at 24.56, up from 18.44 a month earlier and below its Nov 5 peak of 28.18. The week itself is light: 17 scheduled reports across the S&P 500, Russell 1000 and core names, concentrated in technology (6) and consumer-cyclical (5), with most dates still estimated.

sections.heading: What to watch
sections.body: Tuesday carries the heaviest load: Analog Devices, Workday, Nutanix and HP Inc. report into a technology group whose median 3-day reaction off recent prints is +0.2%, while Best Buy, Burlington and Dick's report into consumer-cyclical at +0.3%. Dollar Tree and J.M. Smucker on Tuesday plug into consumer-defensive, where the median is -0.5%. Monday opens with Hewlett Packard Enterprise and Zoom (technology) plus Jacobs and Amentum (industrials, +0.3%). Wednesday has Deere and Williams-Sonoma. Gap is listed for Thursday, a US market holiday, so that date is likely an estimate.

sections.heading: Signals to trust
sections.body: Mining (+4.6% median, 215 tickers, 2,766 news items) leads the reaction table, with copper the other way at -2.5% on 6 names and 231 items. Energy follows at +2.0% on 315 tickers with 5,138 items, a thick news window. None of this week's scheduled reporters sit in those three sectors, so treat them as backdrop rather than read-through to the prints; the sectors that do report are all within about 0.5% of flat.
